[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Day and Night: Conversations with Sapphic Desire (cranes-day-and-night). The verses the casting arrives at (unit 147–unit 152):

came in [...]
I said, "O lord, [...]
by the blessed [goddess]
I take no pleasure in being
above the earth; a longing
grips me to die
and see the dewy, lotus-
covered banks of Acheron [...]"

I have gone grey at the temples,
yes, and my head is white;
graceful youth has departed,
and my teeth are old.

Of sweet life now
little time is left.

And so I sob often,
fearing Tartarus:
the cellar of Hades is terrible,
and the descent painful,

and for one who goes down,
there is no way back.

Lord, with whom Love, the conqueror,
and blue-eyed Nymphs
and rosy Aphrodite
play together,

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «Will there be a return on what was broken?». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The casting is open.\n\nWhat the rotation arrives at is the late fifth movement of *Day and Night* — the *Middle Night* section — but here drawn together from its scattered positions into a single column of descent: the wish for death before death comes, the grey temples and old teeth, the little time remaining, the sob before Tartarus, and then — last, unresolved — the gods at play together, Aphrodite and the Nymphs and Love, as if the poem cannot end in the cellar but also cannot pretend the cellar is not there. The question you carry is *will there be a return on what was broken*, and these verses are the archive's answer to that question before any transform touches them: a voice that asks the same question, does not receive it, and closes on the image of divine play continuing regardless. The operator will traverse the axis these verses have already declared and then closed: the cost borne in the body, the foreclosure the body enacts, and whatever the verses could not bring themselves to name on the other side of descent. Rebekah Cranes holds this text. The transform is hers.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:0055"}}]}
